subject: Temporary retain runbook and subprocessor onboarding — clarifications
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary retain runbook and subprocessor onboarding — HaleBio ask

Hi team,

HaleBio's security team sent an urgent request this morning: they're doing a regulated audit and have asked us to hold deletion of customer logs and backups for a 45-day window for a scoped subset of their tenant data. They want a short runbook that shows the temporary-retain workflow (who authorizes, how we stop purge jobs, how we isolate snapshots) and evidence that any subprocessors handling backups have been onboarded/attested.

I've drafted a runbook (attached: runbook-draft-v1.md) and pulled together the onboarding checklist (subproc-onboarding-checklist.xlsx). Can you each weigh in on two specific points:

- Karthik: confirm whether the hold will suspend our automated purge pipeline (Helix/backup-pruner) immediately or if we need an ops ticket to stage a freeze. Also confirm which cloud snapshot tiers (hot/cold) the hold must apply to.
- Marissa: can you confirm what evidence HaleBio wants for subprocessor attestation (SOC 2 report, contractual addendum, or completed onboarding checklist)? They copied their counsel (Maya Singh) and will expect a concise packet.

Ben, please help by pulling the subprocessor mapping for the affected services (snapshot storage, log aggregation, and analytics index). We should aim to get a consolidated packet to HaleBio by EOD Thursday.

Attachments: runbook-draft-v1.md, subproc-onboarding-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retain runbook and subprocessor onboarding — HaleBio ask

Thanks Sofia — quick clarifying Qs before I lock anything down:

1) Purge pipeline behavior: the automated purge is Helix-triggered. We can flip a tenant-level flag to skip purge cycles (preferred) OR pause the orchestrator (more global). Tenant flag is safer (scoped) but requires a DB update and a brief redeploy to propagate. Which do we want? If legal wants auditable authorization, I recommend a two-step: (a) tenant-level freeze + (b) ticketed ops pause on the pruner for 48 hrs as fallback.

2) Snapshots: do they want the hold to include cold-tier object storage (S3 Glacier/nearline) or just hot snapshots and aggregated log indices? HaleBio's note said "backups and logs" without tiering — we should confirm. Cold-tier holds have cost and legal implications (longer-term storage billing + potential crossborder retention).

3) Cross-border logs: if any of their data lives in EU regions, we need to confirm whether the hold applies globally or only US-based data; that will affect subprocessor attestations and data transfer paperwork.

Ben: can you attach the subprocessor mapping + which regions each service stores replication in?

I'll sketch the freeze steps once we decide tenant-flag vs orchestrator pause.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product — Platform

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retain runbook and subprocessor onboarding — HaleBio ask

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 09:12 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> HaleBio's security team sent an urgent request this morning: they're doing a regulated audit and have asked us to hold deletion of customer logs and backups for a 45-day window for a scoped subset of their tenant data.

Sofia — thanks for the draft. I spoke briefly with Legal (Maya copied here via HaleBio) yesterday about what typically satisfies these requests. For most audit holds we include:

- A signed amendment (DPA addendum / retention hold annex) that states the duration and scope.
- A pre-auth token (email trail) from the customer's security or legal lead authorizing the hold.
- Evidence of subprocessor compliance: redacted SOC 2 Type II (if available) OR completed onboarding checklist + point-in-time attestation from vendor security contact.

I've attached a short Q&A they asked for (HaleBio_SOC2_QA.pdf) that shows the level of detail they want. Quick summary / my recommendations:

- Purge pipeline: do tenant-level freeze + ops ticketed compensating control. Document the freeze in the runbook and add an approval gate (security manager + product owner).
- Snapshots: include hot and warm snapshots; exclude deep-archive (cold) unless HaleBio explicitly asks — if they ask, we need procurement signoff for cost and a documented justification.
- Cross-border: confirm with HaleBio whether the hold applies to EU replicas. If yes, we must add EU subprocessor attestations and check transfer mechanisms (SCCs).

I'll push a revised runbook integrating the approval gate and the evidence checklist. Attaching HaleBio_SOC2_QA.pdf and my inline comments in runbook-draft-v1.md (see Drive link).

Marissa Cole
Legal Ops — Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HaleBio Security <security@halebio.com>, Maya Singh <maya@cobalt-legal.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary retain runbook and subprocessor onboarding — HaleBio ask

Thanks for the fast turn. Summary and next steps so HaleBio and internal teams are aligned: 

1) Scope: hold applies to logs and hot/warm snapshots for the tenant IDs listed in HaleBio's attachment (we'll confirm the tenant list with them). Cold-archive (deep glacier) is excluded unless they explicitly request — we'll escalate cost/contract.

2) Workflow: we will implement a tenant-level freeze flag (Karthik to implement DB flag + short redeploy) AND raise an ops ticket to pause the global pruner for a 48-hr window as a safety fallback. Approval gate = Security Manager (Sofia) + Product Owner (Karthik).

3) Subprocessor evidence: Marissa to provide either redacted SOC 2 Type II or the completed onboarding checklist + attestation from vendor security contact. HaleBio, please confirm if an SCC/data transfer clause is required for EU replicas.

4) Deliverables & timeline: consolidated packet (runbook PDF, subproc attestations, signed addendum) — target EOD Thursday 2026-09-16. I created Jira ticket RED-4821 and a Drive folder (link below).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHaleBio-Retention
Jira: RED-4821

Ben: Ben, can you drop the subprocessor mapping and region replication table into the Drive folder by EOD Monday so Legal can start their review.

HaleBio (security@halebio.com) / Maya — please confirm the tenant list and whether EU replicas are in-scope. If there's a preferred authorizer for the signed addendum, let us know.

I'll update the runbook with a short audit-trail section and attach the final packet when ready.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: consolidated-runbook-v1.pdf (to follow), subproc-onboarding-checklist.xlsx
